title: Knowledge check: Creating Application Error Classes

questions.prompt: In Creating Application Error Classes, which statement best describes Custom application errors?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.
This option describes a different concept and does not define custom application errors (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.
questions.explanation: Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Creating Application Error Classes?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Centralize expected errors and forward unexpected failures to Express. Log enough structured context to diagnose a problem without recording credentials or unnecessary personal data; do not expose stack traces to clients.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Centralize expected errors and forward unexpected failures to Express. Log enough structured context to diagnose a problem without recording credentials or unnecessary personal data; do not expose stack traces to clients.
questions.explanation: Centralize expected errors and forward unexpected failures to Express. Log enough structured context to diagnose a problem without recording credentials or unnecessary personal data; do not expose stack traces to clients.

questions.prompt: A change related to Creating Application Error Classes appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
